plans.goal: Remove the native header panel from the terminal window and change KitCode's primary color from matcha green to #fc0a0a across the dashboard, mini window, and terminal.
Remove the standalone `kitcode mini` command and `/mini` route, then fold the mini, progress, dynamic-island, and watch-style glance surfaces into switchable view modes inside `kitcode terminal`.

Make direct KitCode integration setup immediately open a one-time native onboarding flow that registers multiple local projects, optionally starts background tracking, and launches one independently switchable companion view: Pet or Mini bar.

Replace the web gateway's Newbie/Hardcore setup split with one concise assistant-led setup path that checks Node.js 20+, requests consent before installing it when absent, then launches KitCode onboarding.
Make `kitcode mini` open as the smallest practical always-on-top micro chip instead of the current large mini dashboard.

Redesign `kitcode mini` from the current tiny 160x64 chip into a more polished fixed-size mini panel that is draggable, not resizable, and opens near the bottom-right of the desktop viewport without sitting too deep on the screen.
Add `kitcode terminal` as a separate Electron terminal-style window that opens centered, can be dragged and resized freely, and provides a safe KitCode-only fake shell with English Vim-inspired UI.

Add a macOS-first KitCode desktop pet whose project-owned visual resources are generated once during implementation with `$hatch-pet`, use #fc0a0a as the primary color, can be dragged anywhere on the desktop as a transparent overlay, stays pinned where dropped like Codex pet behavior, and is shown or hidden only through a PET toggle inside the KitCode Terminal window.

Fix the KitCode desktop pet so it behaves like the Codex pet: clicking the pet grabs it for drag instead of clicking through to apps behind it, dropping pins it in place, and default animation stays quiet and state-driven instead of looping arbitrary motion.

Redesign the KitCode Setup mini window as a terminal/Vim-style experience consistent with KitCode Terminal, with an accessible YES/NO auto-track selector and clear cumulative management of multiple tracked projects.
